page: Amazon Web Services c7i.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs spread across 2 physical execution cores running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The compute architecture integrates 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, AMX-tile, and AMX-int8, alongside hardware cryptographic engines such as AES and SHA-NI.

The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, requiring attached Amazon Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data needs. Network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark evaluations reflect steady single-threaded compute efficiency alongside constrained multi-core capacity due to its 2 physical cores. Stress-ng single-core performance registers an average score of 1990.39, complemented by a Geekbench single-core score of 1845.0. Multi-core performance scales to a Geekbench multi-core score of 4017.0 and a stress-ng score of 4030.98, falling into lower benchmark percentiles. PassMark memory testing indicates lower throughput at 974.88 points, with large-block memory read bandwidth achieving 23.54 GB/s. In workload-specific testing, static web serving reaches 7.34 GB/s throughput, and small 135M parameter LLM inference delivers 475.56 prompt processing tokens per second and 103.18 text generation tokens per second.

The c7i.xlarge delivers cost-efficient compute capacity for workloads that demand modern vector execution and single-threaded performance without requiring large memory allocations. Tradeoffs center on the limited 8.0 GB DDR5 capacity and lack of local NVMe storage. The instance aligns best with frontend web servers, API routing services, small-scale batch computation, lightweight Clang compilation tasks, and microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by custom 4th Generation Intel Xeon 8488C processors within the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores clocked at 3.2 GHz, 105 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no bundled local storage and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks highlight consistent single-threaded processing alongside predictable throughput in static web serving at 7.34 GB/s and lightweight inference tasks. The instance serves cost-effective execution for web servers, CI/CD worker nodes, microservices, and lightweight batch workloads needing modern x86_64 vector instructions without intensive memory or local storage requirements.
